title: Initiative: Tiered SLO definitions + error budget policy (Hosted vs Dedicated)
creator: Sean Gallagher
project: Tiered SLO definitions + error budget policy
description:
Umbrella initiative to formalize tier-aware SLOs + error budget policy and to make budget burn actionable through alerting + enforcement.

Why now
- We have recurring reliability regressions where we only “feel” issues after customer escalation. We need a leading indicator (burn) and consistent tier semantics so the platform responds predictably.
- Dedicated customers are holding us to expectations that differ materially from Hosted multi-tenant behavior; we need explicit targets + dedicated-only indicators (pool readiness).

Scope (v1)
- Define and publish canonical SLOs for Hosted API + Dedicated: success rate/availability, 5xx, timeouts, streaming disconnect rate, p95/p99 latency.
- Standardize SLI definitions (what counts, exclusions, streaming taxonomy).
- Burn-rate alerting standard + dashboards per tier/region/model/route.
- Enforcement mechanisms: deploy/rollout gates consult current budget status; canary analysis tags budget risk; routing can degrade gracefully (fallbacks, failover, protective throttling).
- Update oncall playbooks and incident/postmortem templates to reference budget burn.

Non-goals
- Contractual SLA changes (handled separately by Legal/RevOps).
- Major runtime architecture rework.
- Private deployments enforcement (document mapping guidance; no gates initially).

Deliverables / Definition of Done
1) Published docs (source of truth)
- Tiered SLO table + definitions (Hosted vs Dedicated) with measurement windows, exclusions, and breakdown dimensions.
- Error budget policy + enforcement playbook (burn thresholds, paging/ticketing, escalation, change restrictions, override process).
- SLI spec (success vs failure classification; timeouts; streaming disconnect taxonomy).

2) Instrumentation + computation
- Canonical tier dimension propagated from request context through gateway → routing → runtime metrics pipeline.
- Error budget computation job/service powering dashboards + gating checks.
- Dedicated readiness SLI emitted (scheduler health + capacity signal).

3) Alerting + dashboards
- Standard SLO dashboards per tier, with consistent naming and filters (tier/region/model/route).
- Burn-rate alerts using multi-window approach; annotations include owner, runbook, mitigation.

4) Enforcement (phased)
- Phase A: warn-only gates in CI/CD + canary tooling for pilot services.
- Phase B: soft-block (requires explicit override token + audit trail).
- Phase C: hard-block when budget exhausted for scoped tier/service.

5) Operational readiness
- Runbook for budget exhaustion response (mitigation checklist: routing fallback, throttling, feature flag rollback, change freeze).
- Comms guidelines (status page triggers and Dedicated vs Hosted templates).

Milestones / Phases
- Phase 0 (baseline + alignment) [target: end of 2026-01]
  - Inventory existing metrics/dashboards, pull last 90d distributions, draft initial targets per tier.
- Phase 1 (definitions + dashboards + alerts) [target: mid 2026-02]
  - Publish docs, compute SLIs, stand up dashboards, enable burn-rate alerts to #eng-sre.
- Phase 2 (enforcement + mitigation) [target: mid 2026-03]
  - Release gates + canary integration + routing degradation rules + protective throttling.
- Phase 3 (tuning + rollout expansion) [ongoing]
  - Reduce alert noise, refine targets, expand gated services.

Risks / Open questions
- Streaming disconnect attribution: client abort vs server-side disconnect; needs consistent gateway + runtime taxonomy to avoid “double punishment” in burn.
- Cardinality budget: per-model/per-route/per-region can blow up. Need explicit label controls and aggregation rules.
- Dedicated SLOs: targets must reflect pool isolation + readiness expectations; avoid paging storms on short readiness dips while still catching true provisioning failures.
- Enforcement rollout: avoid blocking urgent fixes; start warn-only and define explicit override criteria + audit TTL.

Success metrics (initial)
- 30–40% reduction in incident volume caused by regressions caught by gates/canary within 8 weeks of Phase 2.
- MTTR improvement via faster triage from standardized dashboards/runbooks.
- Reduced “dashboard vs customer observed” disputes by clarifying SLI exclusions and fixing misattribution.

Next steps
- Finalize v1 SLO targets after backtest (Q4/Q1) and publish as canonical tables.
- Turn on burn alerts in ticket mode for 1 week, then page mode for P0 customer journeys.
- Pilot gates on API gateway + routing services; define rollback criteria and override workflow.
